pg.quote: Mellow Yellow … This underwater spectacle reaches depths between 10 to 30 m.

dwwb.quote: Mellow Yellow is named after the vast numbers of yellow soft corals that cover the current facing is the pinnacle.

da.quote: A sea of gold anthias, crimson sea fans and blue water add even more colour to this dive.

highlights.text: Yellow soft corals cover the current-facing side
Thick schools of anthias and crimson sea fans

summary.text: A Bligh Water pinnacle named for the yellow soft corals that smother its current-facing side. Anthias swarm around the rock and sea fans add colour, so it is best dived with some water movement.

pg.quote: At 18-30 m, this dive site is best for seasoned divers.

da.quote: Named for the massive bushes of black corals blanketing this soaring pinnacle.

highlights.text: Schools of big-eye jacks, barracuda and fusiliers
Black coral bushes cover the pinnacle

summary.text: A tall Bligh Water pinnacle dived by experienced divers. It is better known for its crowds of schooling fish than for coral, with sharks and eagle rays often passing.

pg.quote: Instant Replay … The depth of this one is 15-25 m.

tas.quote: a wall of red and yellow soft corals so dense, waving softly in the current

highlights.text: Dense red and yellow soft coral wall
Nudibranchs and pygmy seahorses for macro

summary.text: A Rakiraki dive along a wall thick with red and yellow soft corals that sway in the current, with small macro life such as nudibranchs among the coral heads.
